_comment: Candidate profile + filtering rules. Edit this file to change preferences; no code changes needed. Values below are an example profile.
_season_note: which year's Summer<year>-Internships lists to pull

candidate.name: Your Name
candidate._work_authorization_note: one of: us_citizen, permanent_resident, f1, h1b, other_sponsorship
candidate._degree_level_note: bachelor / master / phd: drives undergrad-only, master's-only, PhD-only filters and the grad-level bonuses
candidate._graduation_note: Any JD graduation window overlapping graduation_earliest..graduation_latest counts as a match.
candidate._preferred_area_note: first-choice area: its jobs get their own report section regardless of score

hard_exclude._comment: Matching any rule => dropped, never shown in the report
hard_exclude._markers_note: 🛂 no sponsorship / 🇺🇸 US citizens only / 🔒 closed
hard_exclude._h1b_note: simplify.jobs data has a sponsors_h1b field; explicitly false => excluded
hard_exclude._grad_note: Excluded when the JD states a graduation window that doesn't overlap the candidate's
hard_exclude._age_note: Only postings from the last N days; postings without a date are excluded too

jd_mismatch._comment: When the full JD is available (simplify source): flag pure-C++ / ML-heavy roles that don't fit the candidate's stack
jd_mismatch._cpp_note: C++ appears but no Python/Java/JavaScript/SQL/web/backend => treated as a C++-only role
jd_mismatch._ml_note: 3+ ML terms (pytorch/tensorflow/model training/transformer...) => treated as an AI/ML role

hard_exclude._regex_note: Substring matching misses 'AI and ML Projects' (no slash) and can't use bare 'ai' (hits email/training/maintain), so these use word-boundary regexes.
hard_exclude._term_note: The off-season README still lists expired terms (e.g. Winter 2026, dead links); terms before min_term_year are excluded.
hard_exclude._data_note: Excludes roles whose function is data (Data Engineer / Analyst / Scientist / Architect, Analytics Engineer, Database Engineer, BI, ETL). 'Software Engineer: Data Platform' is kept: it's a SWE role on a data team. Add r'\bdata platform' to exclude those too.
hard_exclude._override_note: If the title also has one of these strong SWE signals, the AI/ML regexes don't apply. Otherwise 'Backend Software Engineer Intern - Java & AI - Masters' gets dropped over one 'AI' (this happened).
hard_exclude._undergrad_note: Undergrad-only postings are excluded. 'undergraduate' contains 'graduate', so anchor on \bundergrad, not grad.
hard_exclude._canada_note: Canada-only postings are excluded (US sponsorship doesn't transfer to Canadian work permits). Multi-location postings that include a US site are kept (e.g. Microsoft Vancouver+Redmond).
hard_exclude._qa_note: The include regexes let in 'Software QA Test Intern', hence this group; it also stops semiconductor 'Test Engineering Intern' roles. 'validation' is deliberately NOT excluded: Tesla's Update Systems Validation is flagged, not dropped.
hard_exclude._title_mismatch_note: verify.py drops a job whose REAL title (from the JD page) matches one of these. setup.py keeps only the families the user didn't pick.

soft_warn._comment: Not excluded, only marked ⚠️: aerospace/defense-adjacent companies whose internships often require US-person status under ITAR. Check the JD's export-control clause before applying.

scoring._comment: Total score 0-100 decides the report bucket
scoring._la_note: Location weights reflect the candidate's preferences: Remote > preferred metro > secondary metros.

stack_match._comment: Title mentions one of these directions => direct fit with a backend/distributed/cloud background

scoring._advanced_degree_note: 🎓 Master's required => smaller applicant pool for an MS candidate, so it's a bonus
scoring._grad_bonus_note: The JD's stated graduation window matches => strong signal, bonus
scoring._grad_title_note: Title says Masters / Graduate-level => smaller pool for an MS candidate, bonus
scoring._li_penalty_note: 64 of 83 LinkedIn JDs never mention work authorization, and the script can't reach the company's own JD (LinkedIn guests get no apply link; guessing ATS slugs hits ~15%). So those postings are down-weighted rather than hidden: most sponsoring companies don't state it either.

cooldown._comment: Companies that cap applications per period; hidden while in cooldown. Example entry below.

groups.reason: example: company allows 2 applications per 6 months

_include_regex_note: The include keywords are fixed phrases ('software engineer', ...), which missed 5 of 18 common titles: Software Graduate Intern / Software Intern / R&D Software Intern / 2027 Summer Intern - Software. These position-independent regexes close the gap. They run last in is_swe, after all exclusions, so they can't bypass any filter.

screening._comment: Read by screener/agents.py: who the eligibility agents screen for.
screening.candidate: an F-1 master's student who would work under CPT
screening._export_note: true when US export licenses are rarely granted for the candidate's nationality; then 'or be eligible to obtain an export license' does not soften an ITAR/EAR requirement.
screening._engine_note: regex (free) or cascade (LLM agents; needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env). run_daily.sh reads this.
